   252	
   253	class ToolObservation(BaseModel):
   254	    """
   255	    Sanitized, model-visible projection of a tool execution.
   256	    Contains ONLY fields permissible in agent prompt context.
   257	    Raw internal execution data, host filesystem paths, subprocess metadata,
   258	    and private provenance are strictly excluded.
   259	    """
   260	    tool_name: str
   261	    status: ToolExecutionStatus
   262	    output_summary: str
   263	    produced_artifacts: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
   264	    new_evidence_count: int = 0
   265	    warnings: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
   266	    error: Optional[str] = None
   267	
   268	
   269	class ToolOutput(BaseModel):
   270	    tool_name: str
   271	    status: ToolExecutionStatus
   272	    duration_seconds: float
   273	    output_summary: str
   274	    produced_artifacts: List[ProducedArtifact] = Field(default_factory=list)
   275	    new_evidence: List[Evidence] = Field(default_factory=list)
   276	    raw_data: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
   277	    warnings: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
   278	    error: Optional[str] = None
   279	
   280	    def to_observation(self) -> ToolObservation:
   281	        """
   282	        Explicit allowlist projection from internal tool output to model-visible observation.
   283	        raw_data, evidence objects and artifact storage locations are never projected. Free-text
   284	        fields are sanitized (host paths, file URLs and tracebacks removed) and size-bounded.
   285	        Sanitization limits leakage only; authorization stays in ToolRegistry / ExecutionBroker.
   286	        """
   287	        produced = [
   288	            f"artifact://{a.id}" if not a.id.startswith("artifact://") else a.id
   289	            for a in self.produced_artifacts[:OBSERVATION_MAX_ARTIFACTS]
   290	        ]
   291	        summary_res = sanitize_model_text_fail_closed(self.output_summary, OBSERVATION_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS)
   292	        warnings = [
   293	            sanitize_model_text_fail_closed(w, OBSERVATION_WARNING_MAX_CHARS).value
   294	            for w in self.warnings[:OBSERVATION_MAX_WARNINGS]
   295	        ]
   296	        if summary_res.status == SanitizationStatus.FAILED:
   297	            warnings.append("[warning: output summary required fail-closed redaction]")
   298	
   299	        error_val = None
   300	        if self.error:
   301	            error_val = sanitize_model_text_fail_closed(self.error, OBSERVATION_ERROR_MAX_CHARS).value
   302	
   303	        return ToolObservation(
   304	            tool_name=self.tool_name,
   305	            status=self.status,
   306	            output_summary=summary_res.value,
   307	            produced_artifacts=produced,
   308	            new_evidence_count=len(self.new_evidence),
   309	            warnings=warnings,
   310	            error=error_val,
   311	        )
   312	
   313	
   314	OBSERVATION_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS = 1500
   315	OBSERVATION_WARNING_MAX_CHARS = 300
   316	OBSERVATION_MAX_WARNINGS = 8
   317	OBSERVATION_ERROR_MAX_CHARS = 300
   318	OBSERVATION_MAX_ARTIFACTS = 32
   319	
   320	# Delimiters the prompt builder places around tool output; tool text may not forge them.
   321	UNTRUSTED_OPEN = "<<<TOOL_OUTPUT untrusted-data>>>"
   322	UNTRUSTED_CLOSE = "<<<END_TOOL_OUTPUT>>>"
   323	
   324	_TRACEBACK_RE = re.compile(r"Traceback \(most recent call last\):.*", re.DOTALL)
   325	_FILE_URL_RE = re.compile(r"file://\S*")
   326	_WINDOWS_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z]:\\[^\s'\"`<>|]*")
   327	# Absolute or home-relative POSIX path. The lookbehind skips URI authorities (artifact://x,
   328	# input://x) and in-word slashes (application/octet-stream, 1/2).
   329	_POSIX_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w:/.~-])~?/[^\s'\"`<>|,;()\[\]{}]+")
   330	
   331	
   332	def sanitize_model_text_fail_closed(text: Optional[str], limit: int) -> SanitizationResult:
   333	    """
   334	    Remove host paths, file URLs, tracebacks and forged delimiters; clip to `limit` characters.
   335	    Fail-closed principle:
   336	      SAFE: no sensitive elements detected, text passed.
   337	      REDACTED: sensitive elements cleanly replaced by safe tokens.
   338	      FAILED: regex failure, unexpected error, or residual sensitive patterns remain ->
   339	              emit deterministic redaction token, NEVER unsanitized original.
   340	    """
   341	    if text is None:
   342	        return SanitizationResult(value="", status=SanitizationStatus.SAFE)
   343	    if not isinstance(text, str):
   344	        text = str(text)
   345	
   346	    findings: List[str] = []
   347	    try:
   348	        working = text
   349	        if _TRACEBACK_RE.search(working):
   350	            findings.append("traceback")
   351	            working = _TRACEBACK_RE.sub("[traceback withheld]", working)
   352	        if _FILE_URL_RE.search(working):
   353	            findings.append("file_url")
   354	            working = _FILE_URL_RE.sub("[file-url-redacted]", working)
   355	        if _WINDOWS_PATH_RE.search(working):
   356	            findings.append("windows_path")
   357	            working = _WINDOWS_PATH_RE.sub("[windows-path-redacted]", working)
   358	        if _POSIX_PATH_RE.search(working):
   359	            findings.append("posix_path")
   360	            working = _POSIX_PATH_RE.sub("[host-path-redacted]", working)
   361	
   362	        working = working.replace("<<<", "<").replace(">>>", ">")
   363	        if len(working) > limit:
   364	            findings.append("truncated")
   365	            working = working[:limit] + "... [truncated]"
   366	
   367	        # Post-sanitization fail-closed safety check
   368	        if _POSIX_PATH_RE.search(working) or _WINDOWS_PATH_RE.search(working) or _FILE_URL_RE.search(working) or _TRACEBACK_RE.search(working):
   369	            return SanitizationResult(
   370	                value="[content redacted - sanitization uncertain]",
   371	                status=SanitizationStatus.FAILED,
   372	                findings=findings + ["residual_sensitive_pattern"],
   373	            )
   374	
   375	        status = SanitizationStatus.REDACTED if findings else SanitizationStatus.SAFE
   376	        return SanitizationResult(value=working, status=status, findings=findings)
   377	    except Exception as ex:
   378	        return SanitizationResult(
   379	            value="[content redacted - sanitization failed]",
   380	            status=SanitizationStatus.FAILED,
   381	            findings=findings + [f"exception:{type(ex).__name__}"],
   382	        )
   383	
   384	
   385	def sanitize_model_text(text: str, limit: int) -> str:
   386	    """Remove host paths, file URLs, tracebacks and forged delimiters; clip to `limit` characters."""
   387	    return sanitize_model_text_fail_closed(text, limit).value

   390	# ============================================================================
   391	# 3. Artifact Handle Resolution (below the tool boundary)
   392	# ============================================================================
   393	
   394	ARTIFACT_URI_SCHEME = "artifact://"
   395	
   396	
   397	class ArtifactHandleError(ValueError):
   398	    """An agent-supplied artifact reference is not a handle registered for this investigation."""
   399	
   400	
   401	def artifact_handle(artifact_id: str) -> str:
   402	    """Format an artifact ID as the opaque handle shown to the agent."""
   403	    return f"{ARTIFACT_URI_SCHEME}{artifact_id}"
   404	
   405	
   406	def resolve_artifact_handle(context: Dict[str, Any], artifact_ref: str) -> str:
   407	    """Resolve an agent-supplied artifact handle to the host path of its verified working copy.
   408	
   409	    Resolution goes through the run's ArtifactStore view (context["artifacts"], a RunArtifacts):
   410	    only artifacts the store holds for the current run resolve. Host filesystem paths, path-like
   411	    references and handles from other runs are rejected. The agent never supplies or sees the path.
   412	    """
   413	    from storage.models import ArtifactIntegrityError, ArtifactNotFoundError
   414	
   415	    artifact_id = artifact_ref[len(ARTIFACT_URI_SCHEME):] if artifact_ref.startswith(ARTIFACT_URI_SCHEME) else artifact_ref
   416	    if not artifact_id or "/" in artifact_id or "\\" in artifact_id or artifact_id in (".", ".."):
   417	        raise ArtifactHandleError(f"'{artifact_ref}' is not an artifact handle; expected artifact://<id>")
   418	    artifacts = context.get("artifacts")
   419	    if artifacts is None:
   420	        raise ArtifactHandleError("No ArtifactStore is bound to this investigation; artifact handles cannot resolve")
   421	    try:
   422	        return str(artifacts.resolve(artifact_id))
   423	    except ArtifactNotFoundError:
   424	        raise ArtifactHandleError(f"Unknown artifact handle '{artifact_handle(artifact_id)}' for this investigation") from None
   425	    except ArtifactIntegrityError as e:
   426	        raise ArtifactHandleError(f"Artifact '{artifact_handle(artifact_id)}' failed integrity verification") from e
   427	
   428	
   429	def artifact_handle_rejection(tool_name: str, start_time: float, err: ArtifactHandleError) -> "ToolOutput":
   430	    return ToolOutput(
   431	        tool_name=tool_name,
   432	        status=ToolExecutionStatus.FAILED,
   433	        duration_seconds=round(time.time() - start_time, 3),
   434	        output_summary=str(err),
   435	        error="ARTIFACT_HANDLE_REJECTED",
   436	    )

   465	        pass

   470	        pass

    75	class ToolRegistry:
    76	    def __init__(self):
    77	        self._tools: Dict[str, BaseTool] = {}
    78	        self._type_adapter = TypeAdapter(ToolCallInput)
    79	
    80	    def register(self, tool: BaseTool) -> None:
    81	        self._tools[tool.name] = tool
    82	        logger.info(f"Registered tool: {tool.name} (v{tool.version}, category: {tool.category})")
    83	
    84	    def register_tool(self, tool: BaseTool) -> None:
    85	        self.register(tool)
    86	
    87	    def get_tool(self, name: str) -> Optional[BaseTool]:
    88	        return self._tools.get(name)
    89	
    90	    def list_tools(self) -> List[str]:
    91	        """Return list of all registered tool names."""
    92	        return list(self._tools.keys())
    93	
    94	    def _get_schema_for_tool(self, tool: BaseTool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    95	        input_model = TOOL_INPUT_MODELS.get(tool.name)
    96	        if input_model:
    97	            model_schema = input_model.model_json_schema()
    98	            properties = {k: v for k, v in model_schema.get("properties", {}).items() if k != "tool"}
    99	            required = [r for r in model_schema.get("required", []) if r != "tool"]
   100	            parameters = {
   101	                "type": "object",
   102	                "properties": properties,
   103	                "required": required,
   104	            }
   105	        else:
   106	            parameters = {
   107	                "type": "object",
   108	                "properties": {
   109	                    "artifact_id": {"type": "string", "description": "Target file or artifact path"},
   110	                },
   111	            }
   112	        return {
   113	            "type": "function",
   114	            "function": {
   115	                "name": tool.name,
   116	                "description": tool.description,
   117	                "parameters": parameters,
   118	            },
   119	        }
   120	
   121	    def get_tools_schema(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   122	        """Returns OpenAI-compatible function calling schemas for all registered tools."""
   123	        return [self._get_schema_for_tool(tool) for tool in self._tools.values()]
   124	
   125	    def discover_capabilities(self) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
   126	        grouped: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
   127	        for tool in self._tools.values():
   128	            cat = tool.family.value.lower()
   129	            if cat not in grouped:
   130	                grouped[cat] = []
   131	            grouped[cat].append(tool.name)
   132	        if "reconstruction" in grouped and "repair_container" not in grouped["reconstruction"]:
   133	            grouped["reconstruction"].append("repair_container")
   134	        return grouped
   135	
   136	    def list_capabilities(self) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
   137	        """Alias for discover_capabilities for contract compatibility."""
   138	        return self.discover_capabilities()
   139	
   140	    def discover_tools(self, family: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
   141	        fam_norm = family.strip().lower()
   142	        tools = []
   143	        for tool in self._tools.values():
   144	            t_fam = tool.family.value.lower()
   145	            if t_fam == fam_norm or (fam_norm == "reconstruction" and tool.name == "repair_container"):
   146	                tools.append({
   147	                    "name": tool.name,
   148	                    "description": tool.description,
   149	                })
   150	        return tools
   151	
   152	    def get_tool_schema(self, tool_name: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
   153	        tool = self.get_tool(tool_name)
   154	        if not tool:
   155	            return None
   156	        return self._get_schema_for_tool(tool)
   157	
   158	    def validate_input(self, raw_input: Dict[str, Any]) -> ToolCallInput:
   159	        """Validates raw dictionary against discriminated union ToolCallInput."""
   160	        return self._type_adapter.validate_python(raw_input)
   161	
   162	    async def execute_tool(self, raw_input: Dict[str, Any], context: Dict[str, Any]) -> ToolOutput:
   163	        """Validate tool input, then execute the registered tool.
   164	
   165	        Fail-closed: input that does not validate against the tool's schema is rejected
   166	        and the tool's execute() is never entered.
   167	        """
   168	        tool_name = raw_input.get("tool") if isinstance(raw_input, dict) else None
   169	
   170	        try:
   171	            validated_input: ToolCallInput = self.validate_input(raw_input)
   172	        except ValidationError as ve:
   173	            logger.warning(f"Rejected tool call '{tool_name}': input validation failed ({ve.error_count()} errors)")
   174	            return ToolOutput(
   175	                tool_name=str(tool_name or "unknown"),
   176	                status=ToolExecutionStatus.FAILED,
   177	                duration_seconds=0.0,
   178	                output_summary=f"Input validation failed for tool '{tool_name}'; the tool was not executed: {ve}",
   179	                error="INPUT_VALIDATION_FAILED",
   180	            )
   181	
   182	        tool = self.get_tool(validated_input.tool)
   183	        if not tool:
   184	            return ToolOutput(
   185	                tool_name=validated_input.tool,
   186	                status=ToolExecutionStatus.FAILED,
   187	                duration_seconds=0.0,
   188	                output_summary=f"Tool '{validated_input.tool}' is not registered in ToolRegistry",
   189	                error="TOOL_NOT_FOUND",
   190	            )
   191	
   192	        if not await tool.is_available():
   193	            return ToolOutput(
   194	                tool_name=tool.name,
   195	                status=ToolExecutionStatus.SKIPPED,
   196	                duration_seconds=0.0,
   197	                output_summary=f"Tool '{tool.name}' is currently unavailable in the environment",
   198	                error="TOOL_UNAVAILABLE",
   199	            )
   200	
   201	        return await tool.execute(validated_input, context)
   202

   325	"""
   326	External-process execution for agent-reachable forensic tools.
   327	
   328	Every external executable a forensic tool launches goes through the ExecutionBroker: policy
   329	resolution (isolation tier, network clamp, timeout ceiling), the workbench allowlist and argument
   330	validators, and the bubblewrap backend. Tools never call subprocess APIs directly.
   331	
   332	The resolved artifact is staged into the run's FORENSIC_WORKSPACE so the sandbox can read it, and
   333	is passed to the command as a path relative to the sandbox working directory; host paths never
   334	appear in the argv.
   335	"""
   336	
   337	from __future__ import annotations
   338	import shutil
   339	from pathlib import Path
   340	from typing import Any, Dict, List
   341	
   342	from execution.models import ExecutionRequest, ExecutionResult, IsolationTier
   343	from workbench.tools import _get_or_create_execution_broker, _get_or_create_resolver
   344	
   345	SANDBOX_CWD_URI = "forensic://"
   346	STAGING_DIR = "staged"
   347	
   348	
   349	def stage_artifact(context: Dict[str, Any], artifact_id: str, host_path: str) -> str:
   350	    """Copy a resolved artifact into FORENSIC_WORKSPACE/staged; return its sandbox-relative path.
   351	
   352	    Always a fresh copy, never a hardlink: the sandbox mounts FORENSIC_WORKSPACE read-write, so a
   353	    linked file would let a sandboxed process rewrite the store's working copy.
   354	    """
   355	    resolver = _get_or_create_resolver(context)
   356	    safe_id = artifact_id.removeprefix("artifact://").replace("/", "_")
   357	    dest = resolver.forensic_root / STAGING_DIR / f"{safe_id}{Path(host_path).suffix}"
   358	    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   359	    if dest.exists():
   360	        dest.unlink()
   361	    shutil.copyfile(host_path, dest)
   362	    return f"{STAGING_DIR}/{dest.name}"
   363	
   364	
   365	async def run_brokered(
   366	    context: Dict[str, Any],
   367	    tool_id: str,
   368	    tool_version: str,
   369	    argv: List[str],
   370	    artifact_id: str,
   371	    timeout_seconds: float,
   372	) -> ExecutionResult:
   373	    """Run an allowlisted external tool through the ExecutionBroker inside the forensic sandbox."""
   374	    resolver = _get_or_create_resolver(context)
   375	    broker = _get_or_create_execution_broker(context, resolver)
   376	    request = ExecutionRequest(
   377	        tool_id=tool_id,
   378	        tool_version=tool_version,
   379	        command=argv,
   380	        cwd_uri=SANDBOX_CWD_URI,
   381	        input_artifacts=[artifact_id.removeprefix("artifact://")],
   382	        network_policy="NETWORK_NONE",
   383	        requested_isolation=IsolationTier.HIGH,
   384	        timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   385	    )
   386	    return await broker.execute(request)
   387

   389	def sandbox_path(context: Dict[str, Any], relative: str) -> Path:
   390	    """Host location of a path the sandboxed command wrote relative to its working directory."""
   391	    return _get_or_create_resolver(context).forensic_root / relative

   394	def execution_provenance(result: ExecutionResult) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   395	    """Internal provenance record for ToolOutput.raw_data (never model-visible)."""
   396	    manifest = result.execution_manifest or {}
   397	    return {
   398	        "execution_id": result.execution_id,
   399	        "tool_id": manifest.get("tool_id"),
   400	        "tool_version": manifest.get("tool_version"),
   401	        "executable_sha256": manifest.get("environment_digest"),
   402	        "command_argv": manifest.get("command_argv"),
   403	        "input_hashes": manifest.get("input_hashes"),
   404	        "requested_isolation": result.requested_isolation.value,
   405	        "effective_isolation": result.effective_isolation.value,
   406	        "backend_id": result.backend_id,
   407	        "network_policy": manifest.get("network_policy"),
   408	        "status": result.status.value,
   409	        "exit_code": result.exit_code,
   410	        "timestamps": result.timestamps,
   411	        "duration_ms": result.metrics.get("duration_ms"),
   412	    }
   413	"""
   414	Run-bound view of the ArtifactStore used by the investigation controller and its tools.
   415	
   416	The ArtifactStore is the only source of artifact identity, content and lineage. This view binds it
   417	to one run and keeps a hash-verified working copy of each artifact on disk, because the forensic
   418	tools parse files. Working copies are independent copies of the CAS blobs: a tool or sandbox that
   419	modifies one cannot change canonical content, and a modified file copy is detected (SHA-256) on the
   420	next resolution, which then fails closed.
   421	"""
   422	
   423	from __future__ import annotations
   424	import hashlib
   425	from pathlib import Path
   426	from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional
   427	
   428	from storage.models import ArtifactIntegrityError, ArtifactNotFoundError, StoredArtifact
   429	from storage.store import ArtifactStore
   430	
   431	
   432	def _file_sha256(path: Path) -> str:
   433	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
   434	    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
   435	        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
   436	            digest.update(chunk)
   437	    return digest.hexdigest()
   438	
   439	
   440	class RunArtifacts:
   441	    """Artifacts of one investigation run: register into the store, resolve handles to working copies."""
   442	
   443	    def __init__(self, store: ArtifactStore, run_id: str, workspace: Path | str, path_resolver: Any = None) -> None:
   444	        if not run_id:
   445	            raise ValueError("RunArtifacts requires a run_id")
   446	        self.store = store
   447	        self.run_id = run_id
   448	        self.workspace = Path(workspace).resolve()
   449	        self.path_resolver = path_resolver
   450	        self._artifacts: Dict[str, StoredArtifact] = {}
   451	        self._paths: Dict[str, Path] = {}
   452	
   453	    async def load_existing(self) -> List[StoredArtifact]:
   454	        """Bind every artifact the store already holds for this run (for example after a restart)."""
   455	        artifacts = await self.store.list_artifacts_for_run(self.run_id)
   456	        for art in artifacts:
   457	            await self._bind(art)
   458	        return artifacts
   459	
   460	    async def register_file(
   461	        self,
   462	        source_path: Path | str,
   463	        artifact_type: str,
   464	        producer: str,
   465	        producer_version: str = "1.0.0",
   466	        artifact_id: Optional[str] = None,
   467	        parent_artifact_ids: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
   468	        produced_by_execution_id: Optional[str] = None,
   469	        produced_by_tool_call_id: Optional[str] = None,
   470	        mime_type: Optional[str] = None,
   471	        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   472	    ) -> StoredArtifact:
   473	        """Ingest a file or directory into the store for this run and bind its working copy."""
   474	        art = await self.store.put_file(
   475	            run_id=self.run_id,
   476	            source_path=source_path,
   477	            artifact_type=artifact_type,
   478	            producer=producer,
   479	            producer_version=producer_version,
   480	            parent_artifact_ids=list(parent_artifact_ids or []),
   481	            produced_by_execution_id=produced_by_execution_id,
   482	            produced_by_tool_call_id=produced_by_tool_call_id,
   483	            mime_type=mime_type,
   484	            metadata=metadata,
   485	            artifact_id=artifact_id,
   486	        )
   487	        await self._bind(art)
   488	        return art
   489	
   490	    async def _bind(self, art: StoredArtifact) -> None:
   491	        path = await self.store.materialize(art.artifact_id, self.run_id, self.workspace)
   492	        self._artifacts[art.artifact_id] = art
   493	        self._paths[art.artifact_id] = path
   494	        if self.path_resolver is not None:
   495	            self.path_resolver.register_artifact(art.artifact_id, path)
   496	
   497	    def ids(self) -> List[str]:
   498	        return list(self._artifacts)
   499	
   500	    def __contains__(self, artifact_id: object) -> bool:
   501	        return artifact_id in self._artifacts
   502	
   503	    def __iter__(self):
   504	        return iter(list(self._artifacts))
   505	
   506	    def __len__(self) -> int:
   507	        return len(self._artifacts)
   508	
   509	    def get(self, handle_or_id: str) -> StoredArtifact:
   510	        artifact_id = ArtifactStore.normalize_id(handle_or_id)
   511	        if artifact_id not in self._artifacts:
   512	            raise ArtifactNotFoundError(f"Unknown artifact handle 'artifact://{artifact_id}' for this investigation")
   513	        return self._artifacts[artifact_id]
   514	
   515	    def all(self) -> List[StoredArtifact]:
   516	        return list(self._artifacts.values())
   517	
   518	    def paths(self) -> Dict[str, Path]:
   519	        return dict(self._paths)
   520	
   521	    def resolve(self, handle_or_id: str) -> Path:
   522	        """Working-copy path for a handle of this run. The path never leaves the tool boundary.
   523	
   524	        Fails closed when a file working copy no longer matches its stored SHA-256.
   525	        """
   526	        art = self.get(handle_or_id)
   527	        path = self._paths[art.artifact_id]
   528	        if art.metadata.get("layout") != "directory" and (not path.is_file() or _file_sha256(path) != art.sha256):
   529	            raise ArtifactIntegrityError(f"Working copy of {art.handle} no longer matches its stored SHA-256")
   530	        return path

--- [Step 39 | THINKING] ---
The demo registry doesn't include get_tool_schema, which limits escalation here, but the full investigation registry allows get_tool_schema to unlock tools like python_exec through progressive discovery. That's intentional design rather than a privilege escalation issue, since all registered tools are already authorized.

I'm also looking at RunArtifacts.resolve for TOCTOU concerns — hash checks happen before reads but directory artifacts skip hash verification entirely. I want to check how register_file ingests tool-provided storage_uri paths, whether _get_or_create_execution_broker is a global singleton with concurrency implications, and review the demo tools themselves: inspect_container, search_strings, run_jadx, find_xrefs, decode_static_payload, and repair_container.

--- [Step 41 | THINKING] ---
I'm noticing that the repair_container logic assumes any encryption bit is fake and clears it unconditionally, even on genuinely encrypted entries, which would make testzip fail CRC checks on real encrypted data and produce an inconclusive result rather than a clean validation.

But the deeper issue is that "Container Evasion Repaired" evidence with RECONSTRUCTED_VERIFIED origin gets emitted into the ledger whenever fixed_entries is non-empty, regardless of whether valid_unzip actually succeeded — so even a failed, invalid repair still injects HIGH-severity "verified" evidence and affects the risk score. I'm also realizing the raw byte scan for ZIP local file headers doesn't respect compressed/stored data boundaries properly when data-descriptor entries (bit 3, csize==0) are present, so it can scan into and "repair" bytes inside embedded payloads like nested APKs/JARs, corrupting legitimate content and breaking its CRC.

Beyond correctness, there's a serious performance problem: the central directory scan walks byte-by-byte through the entire file rather than skipping over local entries using their compressed sizes, so a 100MB APK could mean on the order of 100 million synchronous Python iterations — blocking the event loop for tens of seconds despite being declared async. On top of that, the repaired artifact is being mislabeled with the ORIGINAL_APK type, which is misleading since it's actually a modified/reconstructed file.

I'm also noticing the evasion-detection logic is overly aggressive — any parse flag or ZipFile error, even from a benign corrupted download, gets flagged as "Container Evasion Detected" with HIGH severity and HIGH confidence, with no differentiation between legitimate anomalies (zip64, data descriptors) and actual evasion techniques. Walking through the demo fixture scenario, this cascades through triage, inspection, and repair stages all tagging things HIGH when some of these cases are likely benign.

I want to actually run this to see what risk level the report produces, since benign samples should be labeled as such — I'll check whether llama-server and a local model are available to test this properly, or fall back to a mock provider. Then I should move on to search_strings, find_xrefs, decode_static_payload, and jadx for the next phase.

--- [Step 43 | THINKING] ---
This is a crucial finding: search_strings only exposes counts to the model via output_summary, never the actual matched strings or contexts from raw_data. The same blindness applies to find_xrefs — the model only sees counts, not actual callers/callees, since raw_data is never projected through to_observation. So the agent's investigation is effectively blind, operating only on counting oracles rather than real content.

Beyond this visibility gap, I'm spotting serious security issues: search_strings runs model-supplied regex with IGNORECASE over potentially the entire decoded DEX text, and Python's re has no timeout — a catastrophic backtracking pattern could hang the whole service synchronously on the event loop thread, since the execution is blocking despite being wrapped in async. There's also an unbounded decompression risk: zf.read(name) has no size cap, so a malicious zip entry claiming a huge size could trigger an OOM kill, and search_strings over a zip reads every matching entry fully without any bound.

I'm also noting find_xrefs runs AnalyzeAPK on the whole APK in-process per call, which is slow and memory-heavy, and it passes model-supplied regex (via method/class patterns) straight into androguard's matching functions, creating another ReDoS surface — the class name escaping only handles `$`, leaving other regex metacharacters exploitable. Error messages are sanitized at projection, so that's handled. Now I'm moving on to look at payload decoding, jadx, and ELF handling.

    22	def compute_bytes_sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    23	    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    24	
    25	
    26	def carve_dex_from_stream(data: bytes, offset: int = 0) -> List[bytes]:
    27	    """Scans stream for dex\\n03X magic and carves full DEX based on header file_size."""
    28	    carved_dex_list: List[bytes] = []
    29	    idx = offset
    30	    while idx < len(data) - 40:
    31	        chunk = data[idx:idx+8]
    32	        if chunk.startswith(b"dex\n03"):
    33	            # In DEX header, offset 32 (0x20) is 4-byte uint32 file_size
    34	            if idx + 36 <= len(data):
    35	                file_size = struct.unpack("<I", data[idx+32:idx+36])[0]
    36	                if 40 <= file_size <= (len(data) - idx):
    37	                    dex_bytes = data[idx:idx+file_size]
    38	                    carved_dex_list.append(dex_bytes)
    39	                    idx += file_size
    40	                    continue
    41	        idx += 1
    42	    return carved_dex_list
    43	
    44	
    45	def xor_transform(data: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes:
    46	    if not key:
    47	        return data
    48	    k_len = len(key)
    49	    return bytes(b ^ key[i % k_len] for i, b in enumerate(data))
    50	
    51	
    52	def rc4_transform(data: bytes, key: bytes) -> bytes:
    53	    """Standard RC4 stream cipher transformation."""
    54	    S = list(range(256))
    55	    j = 0
    56	    for i in range(256):
    57	        j = (j + S[i] + key[i % len(key)]) % 256
    58	        S[i], S[j] = S[j], S[i]
    59	
    60	    i = j = 0
    61	    res = bytearray()
    62	    for byte in data:
    63	        i = (i + 1) % 256
    64	        j = (j + S[i]) % 256
    65	        S[i], S[j] = S[j], S[i]
    66	        k = S[(S[i] + S[j]) % 256]
    67	        res.append(byte ^ k)
    68	    return bytes(res)
    69

   222	                    storage_uri=str(elf_out_path),

   226	                    producer_version=self.version,
   227	                )
   228	            )

   232	                    run_id=context.get("run_id", "manual"),

   241	                    severity=EvidenceSeverity.HIGH,

   251	            status = ToolExecutionStatus.SUCCESS

   289	class JadxTool(BaseTool):
   290	    name: str = "run_jadx"
   291	    family = ToolFamily.BYTECODE
   292	    version: str = "1.5.0"
   293	    category: str = "bytecode"
   294	    description: str = "Decompiles APK or DEX bytecode into Java source code with deobfuscation support."
   295	    execution_mode = ToolExecutionMode.EXTERNAL_PROCESS

   305	
   306	    async def execute(self, tool_input: RunJadxInput, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> ToolOutput:
   307	        start_time = time.time()
   308	        try:
   309	            artifact_path = resolve_artifact_handle(context, tool_input.artifact_id)
   310	        except ArtifactHandleError as e:
   311	            return artifact_handle_rejection(self.name, start_time, e)
   312	
   313	        if not os.path.exists(artifact_path):
   314	            return ToolOutput(
   315	                tool_name=self.name,
   316	                status=ToolExecutionStatus.FAILED,
   317	                duration_seconds=round(time.time() - start_time, 3),
   318	                output_summary=f"Artifact not found on disk: {tool_input.artifact_id}",
   319	                error="ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND",

   321	
   322	        try:

   324	            out_rel = f"jadx/{Path(staged).stem}_{int(time.time())}"
   325	            argv = ["jadx", "-d", out_rel, "--no-res", "-j", "4"]

   340	                )

   344	            java_files = list(sources_dir.rglob("*.java")) if sources_dir.exists() else []
   345

   347	            if java_files:

   350	                        artifact_type=ArtifactType.DECOMPILED_JAVA,
   351	                        storage_uri=str(sources_dir),

   356	                    )

   360	            return ToolOutput(
   361	                tool_name=self.name,
   362	                status=ToolExecutionStatus.SUCCESS if java_files else ToolExecutionStatus.INCONCLUSIVE,
   363	                duration_seconds=round(time.time() - start_time, 3),

   371	                },
   372	            )

   378	                duration_seconds=round(time.time() - start_time, 3),

   380	                error=str(e),
   381	            )

   189	    "frida_dynamic_trace": IsolationTier.CRITICAL,
   190	}
   191

   193	NETWORK_ALLOWED_TOOLS: set[str] = set()
   194	
   195	
   196	# ============================================================================
   197	# 2. Resolved Execution Policy Model
   198	# ============================================================================
   199	
   200	class ResolvedExecutionPolicy(BaseModel):
   201	    """
   202	    Immutable specification of effective execution parameters resolved by ExecutionPolicy.
   203	    Agent request values have been evaluated, clamped, or overridden by policy authority.
   204	    """
   205	    tool_id: str
   206	    requested_isolation: IsolationTier
   207	    policy_required_isolation: IsolationTier
   208	    effective_isolation: IsolationTier
   209	    effective_network_policy: str = "NETWORK_NONE"
   210	    effective_filesystem_policy: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
   211	    effective_resource_class: str = "STANDARD"
   212	    effective_timeout_seconds: float = 30.0
   213	    requires_high_assurance: bool = False
   214	    warnings: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
   215	
   216	
   217	# ============================================================================
   218	# 3. Execution Policy Evaluator
   219	# ============================================================================
   220	
   221	class ExecutionPolicy:
   222	    """
   223	    Evaluates ExecutionRequests against system invariants:
   224	    1. Tier Escalation: policy may escalate isolation; agent can NEVER downgrade.
   225	    2. Request Neutralization: filesystem, network, and resource settings from the agent
   226	       are requests, not authority.
   227	    3. Fail Closed: CRITICAL operations require verified high-assurance isolation.
   228	    """
   229	
   230	    def __init__(
   231	        self,
   232	        default_required_tier: IsolationTier = IsolationTier.HIGH,
   233	        max_timeout_seconds: float = 300.0,
   234	        enforce_no_network: bool = True,
   235	    ):
   236	        self.default_required_tier = default_required_tier
   237	        self.max_timeout_seconds = max_timeout_seconds
   238	        self.enforce_no_network = enforce_no_network
   239	
   240	    def resolve(self, request: ExecutionRequest) -> ResolvedExecutionPolicy:
   241	        """
   242	        Evaluate and resolve an ExecutionRequest into a concrete ResolvedExecutionPolicy.
   243	        """
   244	        warnings: List[str] = []
   245	
   246	        # 1. Determine Policy Required Isolation Tier
   247	        policy_required = TOOL_MINIMUM_ISOLATION.get(request.tool_id, self.default_required_tier)
   248	
   249	        # 2. Tier Escalation Invariant:
   250	        # Effective tier is max(requested, policy_required).
   251	        # Agent can elevate to higher isolation, but cannot downgrade below policy_required.
   252	        if request.requested_isolation < policy_required:
   253	            effective_tier = policy_required
   254	            warnings.append(
   255	                f"Requested isolation tier {request.requested_isolation.value} escalated to "
   256	                f"{policy_required.value} by execution policy for tool '{request.tool_id}'."
   257	            )
   258	        else:
   259	            effective_tier = request.requested_isolation
   260	
   261	        # 3. Network Policy Authority:
   262	        # Agent network requests are not authority. Unless tool is in NETWORK_ALLOWED_TOOLS,
   263	        # network access is denied (clamped to NETWORK_NONE).
   264	        effective_network = "NETWORK_NONE"
   265	        if request.network_policy and request.network_policy != "NETWORK_NONE":
   266	            if request.tool_id not in NETWORK_ALLOWED_TOOLS or self.enforce_no_network:
   267	                warnings.append(
   268	                    f"Agent requested network policy '{request.network_policy}' denied by policy; "
   269	                    "forced to NETWORK_NONE."
   270	                )
   271	                effective_network = "NETWORK_NONE"
   272	            else:
   273	                effective_network = request.network_policy
   274	
   275	        # 4. Filesystem Policy Authority:
   276	        # Prevent unauthorized write requests or escaping beyond forensic domain.
   277	        effective_fs: Dict[str, Any] = {
   278	            "cwd_uri": request.cwd_uri,
   279	            "read_domains": ["input", "forensic", "artifact"],
   280	            "write_domains": ["forensic", "artifact"],
   281	        }
   282	        if request.cwd_uri.startswith("input://"):
   283	            # Writes inside input:// are strictly prohibited
   284	            warnings.append("Requested working directory inside input:// domain; clamped to forensic://work.")
   285	            effective_fs["cwd_uri"] = "forensic://work"
   286	
   287	        # 5. Resource Limits Authority:
   288	        # Clamp timeout to max_timeout_seconds
   289	        effective_timeout = min(request.timeout_seconds, self.max_timeout_seconds)
   290	        if request.timeout_seconds > self.max_timeout_seconds:
   291	            warnings.append(
   292	                f"Requested timeout {request.timeout_seconds}s exceeds ceiling {self.max_timeout_seconds}s; "
   293	                f"clamped to {effective_timeout}s."
   294	            )
   295	
   296	        effective_res_class = request.resource_class or "STANDARD"
   297	
   298	        requires_high_assurance = (effective_tier == IsolationTier.CRITICAL)
   299	
   300	        return ResolvedExecutionPolicy(
   301	            tool_id=request.tool_id,
   302	            requested_isolation=request.requested_isolation,
   303	            policy_required_isolation=policy_required,
   304	            effective_isolation=effective_tier,
   305	            effective_network_policy=effective_network,
   306	            effective_filesystem_policy=effective_fs,
   307	            effective_resource_class=effective_res_class,
   308	            effective_timeout_seconds=effective_timeout,
   309	            requires_high_assurance=requires_high_assurance,
   310	            warnings=warnings,
   311	        )
   312	"""
   313	KAVACH AI 2.0 - BackendResolver.
   314	Resolves concrete execution backend from resolved IsolationTier and runtime availability.
   315	Enforces fail-closed isolation security: CRITICAL requests never downgrade to Bwrap.
   316	"""
   317	
   318	from __future__ import annotations
   319	import logging
   320	from typing import Dict, Optional, Set
   321	from execution.models import IsolationTier
   322	from execution.backends.base import BaseExecutionBackend
   323	
   324	logger = logging.getLogger("kavach.execution.resolver")
   325	
   326	
   327	class NoAvailableBackendError(RuntimeError):
   328	    """Raised when no registered backend satisfies the required isolation tier."""
   329	    pass
   330	
   331	
   332	class BackendResolver:
   333	    """
   334	    Manages registered execution backends and maps effective IsolationTiers to
   335	    concrete backends based on host availability and security policy.
   336	    """
   337	
   338	    def __init__(self, backends: Optional[Dict[str, BaseExecutionBackend]] = None):
   339	        self._backends: Dict[str, BaseExecutionBackend] = dict(backends or {})
   340	
   341	    def register_backend(self, backend: BaseExecutionBackend) -> None:
   342	        """Register a new backend instance."""
   343	        self._backends[backend.backend_id] = backend
   344	
   345	    def get_backend(self, backend_id: str) -> Optional[BaseExecutionBackend]:
   346	        """Direct retrieval by backend identifier."""
   347	        return self._backends.get(backend_id)
   348	
   349	    async def resolve_backend(self, tier: IsolationTier) -> Optional[BaseExecutionBackend]:
   350	        """
   351	        Resolve an available execution backend that satisfies the requested IsolationTier.
   352	
   353	        Security Invariant:
   354	        - If tier is CRITICAL, and no backend declares CRITICAL support, return None (or fail closed).
   355	          NEVER fall back to bwrap or a lower-assurance backend.
   356	        """
   357	        for backend_id, backend in self._backends.items():
   358	            if tier in backend.supported_tiers:
   359	                if await backend.is_available():
   360	                    return backend
   361	                else:
   362	                    logger.warning(f"Backend '{backend_id}' supports tier '{tier.value}' but reported unavailable.")
   363	
   364	        # No backend found that legitimately supports this tier
   365	        if tier == IsolationTier.CRITICAL:
   366	            logger.error(
   367	                "CRITICAL isolation tier required, but no compliant high-assurance backend "
   368	                "(microVM/hypervisor) is registered or available. Failing closed without downgrade."
   369	            )
   370	        return None
   371	
   372	    def list_supported_tiers(self) -> Set[IsolationTier]:
   373	        """Return the union of all isolation tiers supported across registered backends."""
   374	        tiers: Set[IsolationTier] = set()
   375	        for backend in self._backends.values():
   376	            tiers.update(backend.supported_tiers)
   377	        return tiers
   378	"""
   379	KAVACH AI 2.0 - Bubblewrap Workbench Execution Backend.
   380	Wraps WorkbenchExecutor to execute ExecutionRequests inside out-of-process
   381	bubblewrap namespaces, RLIMIT constraints, and three-domain filesystem bounds.
   382	"""
   383	
   384	from __future__ import annotations
   385	import os
   386	import time
   387	import uuid
   388	import hashlib
   389	import datetime
   390	from pathlib import Path
   391	from typing import Set, Dict, Any, Optional
   392	
   393	from execution.models import (
   394	    IsolationTier,
   395	    ExecutionStatus,
   396	    ExecutionRequest,
   397	    ExecutionManifest,
   398	    ExecutionResult,
   399	)
   400	from execution.policy import ResolvedExecutionPolicy
   401	from execution.backends.base import BaseExecutionBackend
   402	from workbench.sandbox import WorkbenchExecutor, ExecutionResult as SandboxResult
   403	from workbench.policy import IsolationProfile, ResourceClass, DEFAULT_RESOURCE_PROFILES
   404	
   405	
   406	class BwrapBackend(BaseExecutionBackend):
   407	    """
   408	    Concrete backend wrapping WorkbenchExecutor.
   409	    Supports LOW, MEDIUM, and HIGH isolation tiers.
   410	    Never satisfies CRITICAL isolation tier.
   411	    """
   412	    backend_id: str = "bwrap"
   413	    supported_tiers: Set[IsolationTier] = {
   414	        IsolationTier.LOW,
   415	        IsolationTier.MEDIUM,
   416	        IsolationTier.HIGH,
   417	    }
   418	
   419	    def __init__(self, executor: WorkbenchExecutor):
   420	        self.executor = executor
   421	
   422	    async def is_available(self) -> bool:
   423	        """Available if the underlying WorkbenchExecutor is initialized."""
   424	        return True
   425	
   426	    def _map_isolation_profile(self, tier: IsolationTier) -> IsolationProfile:
   427	        """Map IsolationTier to workbench sandbox IsolationProfile."""
   428	        if tier == IsolationTier.LOW and self.executor.policy.allow_normal_profile:
   429	            return IsolationProfile.NORMAL
   430	        # MEDIUM and HIGH use HARDENED (bwrap namespaces + unshare-all + unshare-net)
   431	        return IsolationProfile.HARDENED
   432	
   433	    def _map_resource_class(self, res_class_str: str) -> ResourceClass:
   434	        """Map resource class string to ResourceClass enum."""
   435	        try:
   436	            return ResourceClass(res_class_str)
   437	        except Exception:
   438	            return ResourceClass.STANDARD
   439	
   440	    def _compute_input_hashes(self, input_artifacts: list[str]) -> Dict[str, str]:
   441	        """Compute SHA256 hashes of input artifacts where accessible on disk."""
   442	        hashes: Dict[str, str] = {}
   443	        for art_ref in input_artifacts:
   444	            try:
   445	                # Check if it's a known artifact ID in resolver
   446	                art_path = self.executor.path_resolver.get_artifact_path(art_ref)
   447	                if art_path and art_path.exists():
   448	                    hashes[art_ref] = hashlib.sha256(art_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
   449	                    continue
   450	                # Check if it's a direct file path or URI
   451	                if os.path.exists(art_ref):
   452	                    hashes[art_ref] = hashlib.sha256(Path(art_ref).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
   453	            except Exception:
   454	                pass
   455	        return hashes
   456	
   457	    async def execute(
   458	        self,
   459	        request: ExecutionRequest,
   460	        resolved_policy: ResolvedExecutionPolicy,
   461	    ) -> ExecutionResult:
   462	        """Execute request via WorkbenchExecutor and return normalized ExecutionResult."""
   463	        start_dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
   464	        start_iso = start_dt.isoformat()
   465	
   466	        exec_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
   467	        profile = self._map_isolation_profile(resolved_policy.effective_isolation)
   468	        res_class = self._map_resource_class(resolved_policy.effective_resource_class)
   469	        timeout = resolved_policy.effective_timeout_seconds
   470	        cwd_uri = resolved_policy.effective_filesystem_policy.get("cwd_uri", request.cwd_uri)
   471	
   472	        # 1. Execute Code or Command
   473	        sandbox_res: SandboxResult
   474	        argv_for_manifest: list[str] = []
   475	
   476	        if request.code is not None:
   477	            argv_for_manifest = ["python3", "-c", "<inline_script>"]
   478	            sandbox_res = await self.executor.run_python(
   479	                code=request.code,
   480	                cwd_uri=cwd_uri,
   481	                timeout=timeout,
   482	                isolation_profile=profile,
   483	                resource_class=res_class,
   484	            )
   485	        else:
   486	            cmd = request.command or request.arguments or []
   487	            argv_for_manifest = list(cmd)
   488	            sandbox_res = await self.executor.run_command(
   489	                cmd=cmd,
   490	                cwd_uri=cwd_uri,
   491	                timeout=timeout,
   492	                isolation_profile=profile,
   493	                resource_class=res_class,
   494	            )
   495	
   496	        end_dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
   497	        end_iso = end_dt.isoformat()
   498	
   499	        # 2. Map Status
   500	        if sandbox_res.status == "timeout":
   501	            status = ExecutionStatus.TIMEOUT
   502	        elif sandbox_res.quota_exceeded:
   503	            status = ExecutionStatus.OOM if "QUOTA" in (sandbox_res.quota_reason or "") else ExecutionStatus.FAILED
   504	        elif sandbox_res.status == "completed" and sandbox_res.exit_code == 0:
   505	            status = ExecutionStatus.SUCCESS
   506	        elif sandbox_res.status == "cancelled":
   507	            status = ExecutionStatus.CANCELLED
   508	        else:
   509	            status = ExecutionStatus.FAILED
   510	
   511	        # 3. Build Provenance Manifest
   512	        limits = DEFAULT_RESOURCE_PROFILES.get(res_class, DEFAULT_RESOURCE_PROFILES[ResourceClass.STANDARD])
   513	        input_hashes = self._compute_input_hashes(request.input_artifacts)
   514	
   515	        manifest = ExecutionManifest(
   516	            execution_id=exec_id,
   517	            tool_id=request.tool_id,
   518	            tool_version=request.tool_version,
   519	            command_argv=argv_for_manifest,
   520	            requested_isolation=request.requested_isolation,
   521	            policy_required_isolation=resolved_policy.policy_required_isolation,
   522	            effective_isolation=resolved_policy.effective_isolation,
   523	            backend_id=self.backend_id,
   524	            input_hashes=input_hashes,
   525	            filesystem_rules=resolved_policy.effective_filesystem_policy,
   526	            network_policy=resolved_policy.effective_network_policy,
   527	            resource_envelope=limits.to_dict(),
   528	            environment_digest=sandbox_res.executable_sha256,
   529	            timestamp_iso=start_iso,
   530	        )
   531	
   532	        # 4. Consolidate Warnings
   533	        all_warnings = list(resolved_policy.warnings)
   534	        if sandbox_res.warnings:
   535	            all_warnings.extend(sandbox_res.warnings)
   536	
   537	        # 5. Output Artifacts
   538	        output_artifacts: list[str] = list(sandbox_res.produced_artifacts)
   539	        if sandbox_res.full_output_artifact_id and sandbox_res.full_output_artifact_id not in output_artifacts:
   540	            output_artifacts.append(sandbox_res.full_output_artifact_id)
   541	
   542	        metrics = {
   543	            "duration_ms": sandbox_res.duration_ms,
   544	            "stdout_bytes": sandbox_res.stdout_bytes,
   545	            "stderr_bytes": sandbox_res.stderr_bytes,
   546	            "resource_usage": sandbox_res.resource_usage,
   547	            "backend": self.backend_id,
   548	        }
   549	
   550	        timestamps = {
   551	            "started_at": start_iso,
   552	            "completed_at": end_iso,
   553	        }
   554	
   555	        error_msg = sandbox_res.stderr if status == ExecutionStatus.FAILED else None
   556	        if sandbox_res.status == "timeout":
   557	            error_msg = f"Execution timed out after {timeout} seconds"
   558	
   559	        return ExecutionResult(
   560	            execution_id=exec_id,
   561	            status=status,
   562	            exit_code=sandbox_res.exit_code,
   563	            stdout=sandbox_res.stdout,
   564	            stderr=sandbox_res.stderr,
   565	            stdout_ref=sandbox_res.stdout_artifact_id,
   566	            stderr_ref=sandbox_res.stderr_artifact_id,
   567	            output_artifacts=output_artifacts,
   568	            requested_isolation=request.requested_isolation,
   569	            policy_required_isolation=resolved_policy.policy_required_isolation,
   570	            effective_isolation=resolved_policy.effective_isolation,
   571	            backend_id=self.backend_id,
   572	            metrics=metrics,
   573	            execution_manifest=manifest.model_dump(),
   574	            timestamps=timestamps,
   575	            warnings=all_warnings,
   576	            error=error_msg,
   577	        )
   578	"""
   579	KAVACH AI 2.0 - Base Execution Backend Protocol.
   580	Abstract contract for out-of-process isolation backends.
   581	"""
   582	
   583	from __future__ import annotations
   584	import abc
   585	from typing import Set
   586	from execution.models import IsolationTier, ExecutionRequest, ExecutionResult
   587	from execution.policy import ResolvedExecutionPolicy
   588	
   589	
   590	class BaseExecutionBackend(abc.ABC):
   591	    """
   592	    Abstract isolation backend capable of executing ExecutionRequests
   593	    under specific IsolationTiers.
   594	    """
   595	    backend_id: str
   596	    supported_tiers: Set[IsolationTier]
   597	
   598	    @abc.abstractmethod
   599	    async def is_available(self) -> bool:
   600	        """Verify host capabilities and dependencies required for this backend."""
   601	        raise NotImplementedError
   602	
   603	    @abc.abstractmethod
   604	    async def execute(
   605	        self,
   606	        request: ExecutionRequest,
   607	        resolved_policy: ResolvedExecutionPolicy,
   608	    ) -> ExecutionResult:
   609	        """Execute request under resolved policy constraints and return ExecutionResult."""
   610	        raise NotImplementedError

    def __init__(
        self,
        path_resolver: PathResolver,
        policy: Optional[WorkbenchPolicy] = None,
        default_timeout: float = 30.0,
        uid: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.path_resolver = path_resolver
        self.policy = policy or WorkbenchPolicy(default_timeout_seconds=default_timeout)
        self.default_timeout = default_timeout
        self.uid = uid
        if self.policy.bwrap_capability and self.policy.bwrap_capability.available:
            self.bwrap_path = self.policy.bwrap_capability.canonical_path
        else:
            self.bwrap_path = shutil.which("bwrap")
        self.python_bin = sys.executable or "/usr/bin/python3"

    @property
    def bwrap_available(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.policy.bwrap_capability and self.policy.bwrap_capability.available)

    def build_sanitized_environment(self, custom_env: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """Produce a clean minimal environment without host credentials, secrets, or poisoning vectors."""
        clean_path = "/opt/kavach/runtime/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
        # Add virtualenv bin if running in virtualenv
        venv_bin = os.path.dirname(self.python_bin)
        if os.path.exists(venv_bin) and venv_bin not in clean_path:
            clean_path = f"{venv_bin}:{clean_path}"

        project_backend = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
        python_paths = [project_backend]
        for p in sys.path:
            if ("site-packages" in p or "dist-packages" in p) and os.path.exists(p):
                if p not in python_paths:
                    python_paths.append(p)

        env: Dict[str, str] = {
            "PATH": clean_path,
            "PYTHONPATH": ":".join(python_paths),
            "PYTHONUNBUFFERED": "1",
            "LANG": "C.UTF-8",
            "LC_ALL": "C.UTF-8",
            "HOME": str(self.path_resolver.forensic_root),
            "KAVACH_INPUT_ROOT": str(self.path_resolver.input_root),
            "KAVACH_FORENSIC_ROOT": str(self.path_resolver.forensic_root),
            "KAVACH_REPAIR_ROOT": str(self.path_resolver.repair_root),
            "KAVACH_ARTIFACT_ROOT": str(self.path_resolver.artifact_root),
            "KAVACH_ALLOW_REPAIR_WORKSPACE": "1" if self.path_resolver.allow_repair_workspace else "0",
        }

        # Selectively permit non-sensitive, non-poisoning custom vars
        if custom_env:
            for k, v in custom_env.items():
                k_upper = k.upper()
                if k_upper in self.DANGEROUS_ENV_VARS or k_upper.startswith("GIT_") or k_upper.startswith("LD_"):
                    logger.warning(f"Sanitizer stripped dangerous environment variable: {k}")
                    continue
                if any(k_upper.startswith(prefix) for prefix in self.SENSITIVE_ENV_PREFIXES):
                    logger.warning(f"Sanitizer stripped sensitive environment key: {k}")
                    continue
                val_str = str(v)
                if any(val_str.startswith(pfx) for pfx in ("AIza", "ghp_", "gho_", "sk-", "bearer ")):
                    logger.warning(f"Sanitizer stripped credential value in: {k}")
                    continue
                env[k] = val_str

        return env

    def _build_rlimit_preexec(self, timeout_sec: float, resource_class: Optional[ResourceClass] = None):
        """Builds preexec function configuring process group and Linux rlimits derived from ResourceClass."""
        import resource
        rc = resource_class or ResourceClass.STANDARD
        limits = DEFAULT_RESOURCE_PROFILES.get(rc, DEFAULT_RESOURCE_PROFILES[ResourceClass.STANDARD])

        # Measure base thread count for current UID if not switching to dedicated UID
        base_threads = 0
        if self.uid is None or self.uid == os.getuid():
            try:
                uid = os.getuid()
                for pid in os.listdir("/proc"):
                    if pid.isdigit():
                        try:
                            st = os.stat(f"/proc/{pid}")
                            if st.st_uid == uid:
                                base_threads += len(os.listdir(f"/proc/{pid}/task"))
                        except (OSError, FileNotFoundError):
                            pass
            except Exception:
                base_threads = 0

        def _preexec():
            # Change UID if non-root UID requested and running as root
            if self.uid is not None and os.getuid() == 0:
                try:
                    os.setuid(self.uid)
                except Exception as ue:
                    logger.error(f"Failed to switch to UID {self.uid}: {ue}")

            # Linux RLIMIT limits
            try:
                # CPU time limit in seconds
                cpu_limit = max(int(timeout_sec) + 5, limits.cpu_seconds)
                resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (cpu_limit, cpu_limit + 5))
            except Exception:
                pass

            try:
                # Dynamic address space limit derived from ResourceClass
                as_limit = limits.as_bytes
                resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (as_limit, as_limit))
            except Exception:
                pass

            try:
                # Concurrently clamp NPROC respecting hard limit and UID baseline
                cur_soft, cur_hard = resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NPROC)
                target_soft = base_threads + limits.nproc
                target_hard = base_threads + limits.nproc * 2
                new_soft = target_soft if cur_soft == resource.RLIM_INFINITY else min(cur_soft, target_soft)
                new_hard = target_hard if cur_hard == resource.RLIM_INFINITY else min(cur_hard, target_hard)
                new_hard = max(new_hard, new_soft)
                resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, (new_soft, new_hard))
            except Exception:
                pass

            try:
                # File write size limit derived from ResourceClass
                fsize_limit = limits.fsize_bytes
                cur_fsoft, cur_fhard = resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE)
                new_fsoft = fsize_limit if cur_fsoft == resource.RLIM_INFINITY else min(cur_fsoft, fsize_limit)
                new_fhard = cur_fhard if cur_fhard != resource.RLIM_INFINITY else fsize_limit
                resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (new_fsoft, new_fhard))
            except Exception:
                pass

            try:
                # File descriptors limit derived from ResourceClass
                cur_nsoft, cur_nhard = resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)
                new_nsoft = limits.nofile if cur_nsoft == resource.RLIM_INFINITY else min(cur_nsoft, limits.nofile)
                new_nhard = limits.nofile * 2 if cur_nhard == resource.RLIM_INFINITY else min(cur_nhard, limits.nofile * 2)
                new_nhard = max(new_nhard, new_nsoft)
                resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (new_nsoft, new_nhard))
            except Exception:
                pass

        return _preexec

    def build_bwrap_command(
        self,
        inner_cmd: List[str],
        cwd_path: Path,
        resource_limits: Optional[ResourceLimits] = None,
    ) -> List[str]:
        """Wrap command with bubblewrap namespaces and minimized filesystem mounts."""
        temp_quota = resource_limits.temp_storage_quota_bytes if resource_limits else (40 * 1024 * 1024)
        bwrap = [
            self.bwrap_path or "bwrap",
            "--ro-bind", "/usr", "/usr",
            "--ro-bind", "/lib", "/lib",
            "--ro-bind", "/bin", "/bin",
            "--proc", "/proc",
            "--dev", "/dev",
            "--new-session",
            "--die-with-parent",
            "--cap-drop", "ALL",
            "--unshare-all",
            "--unshare-net",
        ]

        if os.path.exists("/lib64"):
            bwrap.extend(["--ro-bind", "/lib64", "/lib64"])

        # Minimal /etc bindings for dynamic linkers and user resolution
        for etc_f in ("/etc/ld.so.cache", "/etc/ld.so.conf", "/etc/ld.so.conf.d", "/etc/alternatives", "/etc/passwd"):
            if os.path.exists(etc_f):
                bwrap.extend(["--ro-bind", etc_f, etc_f])

        # tmpfs /tmp with explicit temp_storage_quota_bytes (--size MUST precede --tmpfs)
        bwrap.extend(["--size", str(temp_quota), "--tmpfs", "/tmp"])

        # Domain bindings
        bwrap.extend([
            "--ro-bind", str(self.path_resolver.input_root), str(self.path_resolver.input_root),
            "--bind", str(self.path_resolver.forensic_root), str(self.path_resolver.forensic_root),
            "--chdir", str(cwd_path),
        ])

        if os.path.exists("/opt/kavach/runtime"):
            bwrap.extend(["--ro-bind", "/opt/kavach/runtime", "/opt/kavach/runtime"])
        elif os.path.exists("/opt/kavach"):
            bwrap.extend(["--ro-bind", "/opt/kavach", "/opt/kavach"])

        bwrap.append("--")
        bwrap.extend(inner_cmd)
        return bwrap

    async def _execute_subprocess(
        self,
        argv: List[str],
        cwd_path: Path,
        cwd_uri: str,
        env: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
        timeout: Optional[float] = None,
        isolation_profile: Optional[IsolationProfile] = None,
        resource_class: Optional[ResourceClass] = None,
        input_bytes: Optional[bytes] = None,
        requested_tool: str = "",
        resolved_path: Optional[str] = None,
        executable_sha256: Optional[str] = None,
        network_policy: str = "NETWORK_NONE",
    ) -> ExecutionResult:
        """Unified internal runner for out-of-process subprocess execution."""
        start_time = time.time()
        exec_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        timeout_sec = min(timeout or self.default_timeout, self.policy.max_timeout_seconds)
        res_class = resource_class or ResourceClass.STANDARD
        limits = DEFAULT_RESOURCE_PROFILES.get(res_class, DEFAULT_RESOURCE_PROFILES[ResourceClass.STANDARD])

        profile = self.policy.decide_isolation_profile(isolation_profile, self.bwrap_available)
        clean_env = self.build_sanitized_environment(env)

        if profile == IsolationProfile.HARDENED and self.bwrap_available:
            final_cmd = self.build_bwrap_command(argv, cwd_path, limits)
        else:
            final_cmd = argv

        # Setup Disk Streaming Sinks with explicit byte quotas
        stdout_art_id = f"tool_stdout_{exec_id[:8]}"
        stderr_art_id = f"tool_stderr_{exec_id[:8]}"
        stdout_path = self.path_resolver.artifact_root / f"{stdout_art_id}.txt"
        stderr_path = self.path_resolver.artifact_root / f"{stderr_art_id}.txt"
        stdout_sink = StreamSink(
            stdout_path,
            max_bytes=limits.stdout_quota_bytes,
            quota_reason=QuotaExceededReason.STDOUT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED,
        )
        stderr_sink = StreamSink(
            stderr_path,
            max_bytes=limits.stderr_quota_bytes,
            quota_reason=QuotaExceededReason.STDERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED,
        )

        # Spawn Subprocess with Dynamic Resource Limits
        preexec = self._build_rlimit_preexec(timeout_sec, res_class)
        logger.info(f"[EXEC-{exec_id[:8]}] Spawning ({profile.value}, {res_class.value}): {' '.join(argv[:6])}")

        proc = None
        timed_out = False
        exit_code = -1
        quota_breached = False
        quota_reason: Optional[QuotaExceededReason] = None

        try:
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                final_cmd[0],
                *final_cmd[1:],
                cwd=str(cwd_path),
                env=clean_env,
                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE if input_bytes else None,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                start_new_session=True,
                preexec_fn=preexec,
            )

            if input_bytes and proc.stdin:
                try:
                    proc.stdin.write(input_bytes)
                    await proc.stdin.drain()
                    proc.stdin.close()
                except Exception:
                    pass

            async def _drain_sink(stream: Optional[asyncio.StreamReader], sink: StreamSink):
                nonlocal quota_breached, quota_reason
                if not stream:
                    return
                try:
                    while True:
                        chunk = await stream.read(8192)
                        if not chunk:
                            break
                        sink.write(chunk)
                except StreamQuotaExceededError as qe:
                    quota_breached = True
                    quota_reason = qe.reason
                    logger.warning(f"[EXEC-{exec_id[:8]}] Stream quota exceeded ({qe.reason.value}). Terminating process group.")
                    if proc and proc.pid:
                        self._kill_process_group(proc.pid)
                except Exception:
                    pass
                finally:
                    sink.close()

            stdout_drain_task = asyncio.create_task(_drain_sink(proc.stdout, stdout_sink))
            stderr_drain_task = asyncio.create_task(_drain_sink(proc.stderr, stderr_sink))

            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), timeout=timeout_sec)
                exit_code = proc.returncode if proc.returncode is not None else 0
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                timed_out = True
                logger.warning(f"[EXEC-{exec_id[:8]}] Timeout after {timeout_sec}s. Terminating process group.")
                self._kill_process_group(proc.pid)
                try:
                    await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), timeout=1.0)
                except Exception:
                    pass
                exit_code = -9

            try:
                await asyncio.wait_for(
                    asyncio.gather(stdout_drain_task, stderr_drain_task, return_exceptions=True),
                    timeout=2.0,
                )
            except Exception:
                pass
            finally:
                stdout_sink.close()
                stderr_sink.close()

            if proc and proc.returncode in (-25, -signal.SIGXFSZ, 153):
                quota_breached = True
                quota_reason = QuotaExceededReason.FILE_SIZE_LIMIT

        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"[EXEC-{exec_id[:8]}] Subprocess execution failed: {e}")
            stdout_sink.close()
            stderr_sink.close()
            if proc and proc.pid:
                self._kill_process_group(proc.pid)
            return ExecutionResult(
                execution_id=exec_id,
                status="failed",
                exit_code=-1,
                stderr=str(e),
                duration_ms=int((time.time() - start_time) * 1000),
                working_directory=cwd_uri,
                isolation_profile=isolation_profile or IsolationProfile.HARDENED,
                effective_isolation=profile,
                requested_tool=requested_tool,
                resolved_executable_path=resolved_path,
                executable_sha256=executable_sha256,
                requested_network_policy=network_policy,
                effective_network_policy="NETWORK_NONE" if profile == IsolationProfile.HARDENED else "NETWORK_ALLOWED",
                resource_class=res_class.value,
                effective_resource_limits=limits.to_dict(),
                backend="bwrap_local" if profile == IsolationProfile.HARDENED else "local_process",
                warnings=[str(e)],
                quota_exceeded=quota_breached,
                quota_reason=quota_reason.value if quota_reason else None,
            )

        duration_ms = int((time.time() - start_time) * 1000)

        if stdout_sink.total_bytes > 0:
            self.path_resolver.register_artifact(stdout_art_id, stdout_path)
        if stderr_sink.total_bytes > 0:
            self.path_resolver.register_artifact(stderr_art_id, stderr_path)

        out_summary, out_preview, out_trunc = AdaptiveOutputCompactor.compact_sink(
            stdout_sink, "stdout", stdout_art_id
        )
        err_summary, err_preview, err_trunc = AdaptiveOutputCompactor.compact_sink(
            stderr_sink, "stderr", stderr_art_id
        )

        status = "timeout" if timed_out else ("failed" if quota_breached else ("completed" if exit_code == 0 else "failed"))
        warnings = []
        if quota_breached:
            warnings.append(f"Execution quota exceeded: {quota_reason.value if quota_reason else 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED'}")
        if timed_out:
            warnings.append(f"Command execution timed out after {timeout_sec} seconds")
        if exit_code != 0 and not timed_out and not quota_breached:
            warnings.append(f"Command returned non-zero exit code: {exit_code}")

        return ExecutionResult(
            execution_id=exec_id,
            status=status,
            exit_code=exit_code,
            stdout=out_summary,
            stderr=err_summary,
            stdout_head=stdout_sink.head_str,
            stdout_tail=stdout_sink.tail_str,
            stderr_head=stderr_sink.head_str,
            stderr_tail=stderr_sink.tail_str,
            stdout_bytes=stdout_sink.total_bytes,
            stderr_bytes=stderr_sink.total_bytes,
            stdout_artifact_id=stdout_art_id if stdout_sink.total_bytes > 0 else None,
            stderr_artifact_id=stderr_art_id if stderr_sink.total_bytes > 0 else None,
            stdout_preview=out_preview,
            stderr_preview=err_preview,
            full_output_artifact_id=stdout_art_id if stdout_sink.total_bytes > 0 else (stderr_art_id if stderr_sink.total_bytes > 0 else None),
            duration_ms=duration_ms,
            working_directory=cwd_uri,
            isolation_profile=isolation_profile or IsolationProfile.HARDENED,
            effective_isolation=profile,
            requested_tool=requested_tool,
            resolved_executable_path=resolved_path,
            executable_sha256=executable_sha256,
            requested_network_policy=network_policy,
            effective_network_policy="NETWORK_NONE" if profile == IsolationProfile.HARDENED else "NETWORK_ALLOWED",
            resource_class=res_class.value,
            effective_resource_limits=limits.to_dict(),
            backend="bwrap_local" if profile == IsolationProfile.HARDENED else "local_process",
            warnings=warnings,
            truncated=(out_trunc or err_trunc or quota_breached),
            quota_exceeded=quota_breached,
            quota_reason=quota_reason.value if quota_reason else None,
        )

        """

--- [Step 51 | THINKING] ---
I'm examining the sandbox setup—it isolates namespaces and binds the system directories read-only while mounting the forensic root as read-write, but I notice the venv and site-packages paths referenced via PYTHONPATH point into the forensic workspace itself, which could be a gap in the isolation.

I'm also wondering if jadx is reachable inside bwrap depending on where KAVACH_JADX_PATH points, since paths outside the bound directories would fail; meanwhile there's no seccomp filter, and I'm checking whether RLIMIT_AS would interfere with JVM startup given jadx's memory needs, plus whether RLIMIT_NPROC behaves correctly across the new user namespace.

Then I'm flagging that using preexec_fn for forking bwrap while asyncio.to_thread runs elsewhere is risky since Python explicitly warns against preexec_fn in multi-threaded processes — a possible deadlock worth noting as medium risk. I'm also confirming the timeout/kill logic works correctly given `--new-session` and `--die-with-parent` semantics, and noting that stdout artifacts get registered for every execution via the artifact root.

But I realize these stdout/stderr "artifacts" actually go through path_resolver.register_artifact, not ArtifactStore — meaning there are two separate artifact registries, and the full tool output referenced by `full_output_artifact_id` in ExecutionResult never actually lands in the content-addressable store or ledger. That's a real provenance gap.

I also note decide_isolation_profile fails closed correctly when bwrap is missing, raising a policy violation rather than silently falling back — good. But BwrapBackend.is_available always returns True even when bwrap isn't present, so a FAILED result can still misreport "HIGH" isolation, which is a minor inconsistency. Now I want to check whether jadx resolution via try_resolve_tool could return a host path outside the bind mounts, which would break the sandboxing guarantees when run_command executes it.

    def _kill_process_group(self, pid: int) -> None:
        """Reliably terminate a process group (tree) with SIGTERM then SIGKILL."""
        try:
            pgid = os.getpgid(pid)
            os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGTERM)
            time.sleep(0.2)
            os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGKILL)
        except (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
            try:
                os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            except Exception:
                pass
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug(f"Error killing process group {pid}: {e}")

# 5. Workbench Policy Engine
# ============================================================================

class WorkbenchPolicy:
    """
    Evaluates permissions for python execution, shell command execution,
    filesystem operations, and isolation profile selection.
    """

    # Forensic allowed CLIs - strictly excludes python and python3
    DEFAULT_ALLOWED_FORENSIC_TOOLS: Set[str] = {
        "file",
        "strings",
        "readelf",
        "nm",
        "objdump",
        "unzip",
        "zip",
        "zipalign",
        "apksigner",
        "jadx",
        "apktool",
        "rizin",
        "rz-bin",
        "rz-ax",
        "capa",
        "floss",
        "yara",
        "yara-x",
        "diff",
        "patch",
        "git",
        "pytest",
    }

    DISALLOWED_BINARIES: Set[str] = {
        "python",
        "python3",
        "rm",
        "sudo",
        "su",
        "bash",
        "sh",
        "zsh",
        "dash",
        "nc",
        "ncat",
        "netcat",
        "curl",
        "wget",
        "ssh",
        "scp",
        "dd",
        "mkfs",
        "chmod",
        "chown",
        "kill",
        "pkill",
        "killall",
    }

    DISALLOWED_SHELL_METACHARS: Set[str] = {";", "&", "|", "`", "$", "<", ">", "\n", "\r"}

    def __init__(
        self,
        allowed_binaries: Optional[Set[str]] = None,
        network_enabled: bool = False,
        allow_normal_profile: bool = False,
        max_timeout_seconds: float = 300.0,
        default_timeout_seconds: float = 30.0,
        max_output_bytes: int = 10 * 1024 * 1024,
    ) -> None:
        self.allowed_binaries = set(allowed_binaries or self.DEFAULT_ALLOWED_FORENSIC_TOOLS)
        # Ensure python and python3 are NEVER in allowed_binaries for shell_exec
        self.allowed_binaries.discard("python")
        self.allowed_binaries.discard("python3")

        self.network_enabled = network_enabled
        self.allow_normal_profile = allow_normal_profile
        self.max_timeout_seconds = max_timeout_seconds
        self.default_timeout_seconds = default_timeout_seconds
        self.max_output_bytes = max_output_bytes

        # Discover and register ToolExecutionSpecs
        self._tool_specs: dict[str, ToolExecutionSpec] = {}
        self._initialize_tool_specs()
        self.tool_specs: Mapping[str, ToolExecutionSpec] = types.MappingProxyType(self._tool_specs)

        # Cache bubblewrap capability probe
        self.bwrap_capability = probe_bwrap_capability()

    def register_tool_spec(self, spec: ToolExecutionSpec) -> None:
        """Register or update a ToolExecutionSpec in the policy registry."""
        if not is_inside_approved_immutable_root(spec.canonical_path):
            raise WorkbenchPolicyViolation(
                f"Tool canonical path '{spec.canonical_path}' is outside approved immutable roots."
            )
        self._tool_specs[spec.logical_name] = spec

    def _initialize_tool_specs(self) -> None:
        """Register ToolExecutionSpecs for all allowed forensic tools with canonical paths and validator IDs."""
        validator_map: dict[str, str] = {

        }

            canonical_path: Optional[str] = None
            resolved_realpath: Optional[str] = None

            for root in APPROVED_IMMUTABLE_ROOTS:
                cand = os.path.join(root, tool_name)
                if os.path.exists(cand) and os.access(cand, os.X_OK):

                    resolved_realpath = os.path.realpath(cand)
